days.title: Sex Chromosomes & Sex Determination
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Describe sex chromosomes.
  • Explain sex determination in humans.
  • Differentiate autosomes from sex chromosomes.
  • Identify disorders of sex chromosome number.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • Autosomes — the 22 pairs of non-sex chromosomes.
  • Sex chromosomes — X and Y chromosomes.
  • XX — female; XY — male.
  • SRY gene — on Y chromosome; triggers male development.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Human Chromosomes

  • Total: 46 chromosomes (23 pairs)
  • 22 pairs = autosomes
  • 1 pair = sex chromosomes (XX or XY)

B. Sex Determination

The father determines the sex of the child — he can pass an X or a Y.

FatherMotherOffspring
XXXX (female)
YXXY (male)

C. Sex Chromosome Disorders

ConditionGenotype
Turner syndromeXO
Klinefelter syndromeXXY
Triple X syndromeXXX

takeaways: Humans have 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.

days.title: X-Linked Inheritance Patterns
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Explain X-linked inheritance.
  • Describe why males are more often affected.
  • Predict offspring from X-linked crosses.
  • Identify X-linked disorders.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • X-linked gene — gene carried on the X chromosome.
  • Hemizygous — males have only one X, so one allele determines the trait.
  • Carrier — a female with one recessive allele who doesn't show the trait.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Why Males Are Affected More

Males have only one X chromosome. If that X carries a recessive allele, the male will show the trait. Females must inherit two recessive alleles to be affected.

B. Examples of X-Linked Recessive Disorders

  • Hemophilia A
  • Red-green color blindness
  • Duchenne muscular dystrophy

C. Cross Example

Carrier mother (XᶜX) × normal father (XY):

  • Daughters: 50% carriers, 50% normal
  • Sons: 50% affected, 50% normal

pairs.right: Only one copy of a gene

days.title: Y-Linked Traits & Sex-Linked Disorders
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Describe Y-linked traits.
  • Explain inheritance patterns of Y-linked traits.
  • Distinguish sex-linked from sex-influenced traits.
  • Identify common sex-linked disorders.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • Y-linked — genes on the Y chromosome.
  • Holandric — passed from father to all sons.
  • Sex-influenced — trait expressed differently in males and females.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Y-Linked Traits

  • Only males have a Y chromosome
  • Traits passed father → all sons
  • Examples: hairy ears, some fertility genes

B. Sex-Influenced Traits

  • Autosomal genes, but expression differs by sex
  • Example: pattern baldness (more common in males)

C. Sex-Linked Disorders (Summary)

DisorderType
Hemophilia AX-linked recessive
Color blindnessX-linked recessive
Duchenne muscular dystrophyX-linked recessive
Hairy earsY-linked
Pattern baldnessSex-influenced

days.title: Recombination & Gene Linkage
days.content:
🎯 Learning Objectives

  • Define genetic recombination.
  • Explain crossing over and its role.
  • Define gene linkage and map units.
  • Interpret recombination frequencies.

🔑 Key Concepts

  • Recombination — new combinations of alleles from crossing over.
  • Linked genes — genes close together on the same chromosome.
  • Map unit (centimorgan) — 1% recombination frequency.

📚 Lesson Content

A. Recombination

During Prophase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes exchange segments (crossing over). This creates new allele combinations.

B. Linked Genes

  • Genes on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together
  • The closer they are, the less likely they'll be separated by crossing over

C. Recombination Frequency

  • RF = (number of recombinants) / (total offspring) × 100%
  • 1% RF = 1 map unit (centimorgan)
  • Used to build genetic maps
